Community Gardens Report

The city's community garden programme grew from 14 to 22 sites this year. More than 600 residents now hold plots, and the waiting list has fallen to about four months.

Volunteers planted 1,200 native shrubs to support pollinators. Early surveys suggest bee activity at the gardens has increased compared with nearby parks.

The main challenge remains water supply. Three sites still depend on a single shared tap, and the council has promised rainwater tanks for all sites by next summer.

The programme will run free composting workshops every first Saturday of the month.
